premise: I paid $135,000 out of my late‑husband’s life insurance to put my granddaughter through dental school after she signed a promissory note agreeing to practice in my low‑income town and provide me free care; upon graduating she joined a cosmetic chain in a wealthy suburb, claimed the note was a ‘sentimental gesture,’ and blocked my calls. I sued on the note, won a $195,000 judgment plus statutory interest, and now that she can’t pay, I garnish $1,200 a month from her salary — every check funds a mobile dental clinic I operate in the very neighborhood she abandoned, with a decal listing her name as the ‘Involuntary Founding Sponsor.’
